purpose: Docusate is used to treat or prevent constipation by making your stools softer and easier to pass. It is often recommended for people who should avoid straining during a bowel movement, such as after surgery or childbirth. It can also help if you are taking medications like pain relievers that tend to cause constipation.
how_it_works: Docusate works by acting like a detergent inside your intestines. It helps water and fats mix into your stool, which makes the stool softer and more moist. This makes it much easier and more comfortable to have a bowel movement without straining.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate docusate very well. Some people may notice mild stomach cramping, nausea, or diarrhea if too much is taken. You might also notice a slightly oily feeling in the rectal area with suppository forms.
warnings: Do not use docusate for more than one week unless your doctor tells you to. If you have stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting, check with your doctor before using it. Avoid taking it at the same time as mineral oil. If you have not had a bowel movement after a week of use, contact your healthcare provider. Keep out of reach of children.
typical_dosing: For adults and children over 12, the usual dose is 50 to 300 mg by mouth once a day or divided into smaller doses. It may take 1 to 3 days to see results. Always drink plenty of water while taking this medication. Follow the directions on the package or as directed by your doctor.
